findings.claim: Pope Pius XI declared in 1930 that “every sexual act must be within a framework of marriage.”
findings.truth: That sentence is not in Casti Connubii (31 December 1930) or any other Pius XI text. The encyclical says: “every use of the faculty given by God for the procreation of new life is the right and the privilege of the married state alone” (section 18).
findings.evidence: vatican.va, Casti Connubii, English text, sections 18 and 54

findings.claim: Same-sex marriage became legal in England and Wales in 2013.
findings.truth: The Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013 got Royal Assent on 17 July 2013, but same-sex marriage became legal on 13 March 2014 and the first weddings were on 29 March 2014.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013, commencement table

findings.claim: Same-sex marriage has been legal in England and Wales since 2013.
findings.truth: Legal from 13 March 2014 under the Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013, commencement table

findings.claim: AQA requires you to explain contrasting beliefs on same-sex relationships with reference to Christianity and at least one other religion.
findings.truth: The requirement is correct, but student-facing text must not name the exam board. Use 'the specification'.

findings.claim: The three contrasting beliefs on same-sex relationships required by AQA are:
findings.truth: Same as F4: the board is named in student-facing text.

findings.claim: The British Humanist Association actively campaigns for LGBTQ+ rights.
findings.truth: The British Humanist Association changed its name to Humanists UK in May 2017.

findings.claim: The four key purposes of families on The spec are: procreation, stability and the protection of children, and educating children in a faith.
findings.truth: The spec lists three purposes of families: procreation; stability and the protection of children; educating children in a faith. The sentence says four, lists three, and the wording 'on The spec' is garbled.

findings.claim: The Sex Discrimination Act (1975) made gender discrimination illegal in the UK. Despite this, it still occurs
findings.truth: The 1975 Act was repealed and replaced by the Equality Act 2010, which is the law today. Lesson 2 already cites the Equality Act 2010, so the unit contradicts itself.

findings.claim: The Sex Discrimination Act (1975) made gender discrimination illegal in the UK, but inequalities persist in areas like pay and senior positions.
findings.truth: Same as F8, repeated in the takeaways.

findings.claim: the Church of England has had female priests since 1994 and female bishops since 2015
findings.truth: The legislation allowing women bishops passed in November 2014; the first woman bishop was consecrated in January 2015. Lesson 5 says 2014 and its knowledge check marks 2014 correct, so a student who revises lesson 2 is marked wrong on the platform's own check.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Ordination of women in the Anglican Communion; lesson 5 knowledge check [1]

findings.claim: “You will never be able to be equal between wives, even if it is your ardent desire” (4:129)
findings.truth: No single translation reads that way. It blends Sahih International ('be equal between wives') with Mohsin Khan ('even if it is your ardent desire'). Mohsin Khan: 'You will never be able to do perfect justice between wives even if it is your ardent desire.'

findings.claim: “Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents” (17:23)
findings.truth: Abdel Haleem reads 'Your Lord has commanded that you should worship none but Him, and that you be kind to your parents.' Lesson 4 quotes the same verse correctly in that translation.
findings.evidence: quran.com API, Abdel Haleem 17:23; lesson 4 content_html

findings.claim: “Lower your wing in humility towards your parents in kindness” (Qur’an 17:24)
findings.truth: Abdel Haleem reads 'lower your wing in humility towards them in kindness'. 'Your parents' has been substituted inside the quotation marks.

findings.claim: so that you could recognise one another” (Qur’an 49:13)
findings.truth: Abdel Haleem reads 'so that you should recognize one another'.

findings.claim: Many Christians also argue that inflammatory Bible and Church teachings about gender roles could be considered out of date
findings.truth: The argument is about traditional teachings, not inflammatory ones. A student copying 'inflammatory' would misdescribe the position.

findings.claim: Revision tip: 'What percentage is given for some Muslim countries?'
findings.truth: The only figure in that box is 71%, and it is the Bristol University finding on Muslim women's unemployment in Britain. No percentage is given for any Muslim country.
findings.evidence: the key fact the tip sits on

findings.claim: Question 2 is labelled '1 mark - Give/Name' but its scheme reads '1 marks for each simple point, up to a maximum of 2 marks.' The stem reads 'Give one religious beliefs'.
findings.truth: Each theme carries one five-part question of 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks, so the second part is worth 1 mark. The scheme must award 1 mark for one point.

findings.claim: Question 2 is labelled '1 mark - Give/Name' but its scheme reads '1 marks for each point, up to 2 marks'. The stem reads 'Give one examples'.
findings.truth: Same as F17.

findings.claim: In the two 6-mark schemes, two identically structured exemplars are scored '(developed point + scripture = 3 marks)' and '(developed point + scripture = 2 marks)', totalling 5 on a 6-mark question.
findings.truth: Both exemplars are a developed point plus an applied source, so both earn 3, totalling 6.
findings.evidence: recomputation against the scheme's own header (1-2 + 1-2 + 1-2 = 6)

findings.claim: In the two 6-mark schemes, the exemplars are scored 'up to 3 marks' and 'up to 2 marks', totalling 5 on a 6-mark question.
findings.truth: Both exemplars should be worth 3 marks: belief, source, development.
findings.evidence: recomputation against the scheme's own header

findings.claim: Cards 4 and 5 are cloze fragments lifted from headings: answer 'Human' for '_____ Sexuality Human sexuality refers to...' and answer 'Pope' for '_____ Pius XI declared in 1930...'.
findings.truth: Card 4's answer appears in its own question, and both are single-word answers on fronts that are not questions; card 5 also repeats the misquotation in F1. Replaced with term cards in the 'What is meant by...' style used in lessons 2 and 4.
findings.evidence: docs/FLASHCARD_RULES.md, validator hard rules and the 'broken fragment' anti-example

findings.claim: Cards 4 and 5 are cloze fragments: answer 'Pope' and answer 'Equality'.
findings.truth: Single-word answers on non-question fronts. Replaced with term cards.

findings.claim: Cards 4 and 5 are cloze fragments: answer 'Gender' for '_____ Equality in Britain Today Gender equality means...' and answer 'Discrimination' for 'Key Fact The Sex _____ Act (1975)...'.
findings.truth: Both answers appear in their own questions, and card 5 leaks the 'Key Fact' label into the front. Replaced with term cards.

findings.claim: Three 4-mark practice questions ask for 'similar' beliefs (lesson 1 Q3 on sex before marriage, lesson 2 Q6 on the extended family, lesson 3 Q6 on sex before marriage), and all five lessons label the 4-mark type 'Explain Similarities & Differences'.
findings.truth: The spec says students must be able to explain CONTRASTING beliefs on contraception, sexual relationships before marriage and same-sex relationships, which is what the 4-mark theme question tests. Against that, the spec prints no question stems and AO1 does cover 'similarities and differences'. Options: (a) leave both stems, (b) relabel the type to the contrasting-beliefs wording and rewrite the three 'similar' stems with contrasting schemes. Recommendation: (b), but it needs new mark schemes, not a surgical edit, so it belongs with the question-type relabel pass.

findings.claim: In Britain, divorce is common - roughly 42% of marriages end in divorce.
findings.truth: 42% is the ONS estimate most often quoted, but later cohort estimates are lower. No verified current figure was found inside this session's budget, so the text is left alone.

findings.claim: Methodist Church: 'responsible contraception is a welcome means towards fulfilment in marriage' (lesson 3); Church of England: 'The family remains the most important grouping human beings have ever developed...' (lesson 4).
findings.truth: Both are standard GCSE textbook quotations but neither was traced to a primary Methodist or Church of England document inside this session's budget. Not corrected.

findings.claim: Two revision tips are garbled: 'Write down what you recall about sex Discrimination Act (1975) made gender' and 'Write down what you recall about christians today see marriage as an equal'.
findings.truth: Broken auto-generated text a student reads. Not a factual error, so left for a style pass.

findings.claim: 'You are expected to know six types of family' and 'Each has a clear definition that the exam board uses'.
findings.truth: The spec names the nuclear and extended family under the nature of families and same-sex parents and polygamy under contemporary issues. Single-parent and blended families are not named, and the spec publishes no definitions of family types. Knowing six does no harm, so no edit.

findings.claim: Every deck in the unit holds 5 cards, and cards 1-3 in each deck run definition-to-term.
findings.truth: FLASHCARD_RULES targets 10-14 cards for RE and tells RE decks to avoid inverted definition-to-term as the default. A deck rebuild is out of scope for a fact-check.

findings.claim: The 12-mark scheme in lesson 4 uses raw band descriptors while lessons 1, 2, 3 and 5 use the house band names.
findings.truth: House vocabulary should be used throughout. Not a factual error.

summary: Five lessons checked; 30 edits across 23 FIX findings, 1 ADJUDICATE, 6 NOTE. The paper structure claims hold: the spec sets one five-part question per theme at 1, 1, 4, 6 and 12 marks, 96 marks plus 3 SPaG, 1 hour 45 minutes, and the lesson question sets match, but two 1-mark schemes awarded 2 and four 6-mark schemes totalled 5. All 25 knowledge check keys and all five multiple-choice keys are correct. The worst content errors are an invented Pius XI quotation, a 'four purposes' box that lists three, the Sex Discrimination Act 1975 taught as current law, and a women-bishops date that contradicts the unit's own knowledge check.
